name: Wolfgang Schäuble

summary.text: Wolfgang Schäuble was Germany's Federal Minister of Finance during the Greek bailouts. In July 2015 a German Finance Ministry paper proposed that Greece could take a five-year 'time-out' from the eurozone, with some debt written off, if it did not improve its bailout proposals; Schäuble said on 14 July 2015 that the idea had broad support within the German government.

sources.title: Schäuble insists that a 'temporary Grexit' is the best solution for Greece
Temporary Grexit had support in German govt. - Schaeuble
Intentionally or otherwise, Schäuble has killed off the prospect of a Grexit

facts.claim: A German Finance Ministry paper in July 2015 argued Greece could take a five-year 'time-out' from the eurozone, with some debt written off, if Athens did not improve its bailout proposals; it presented tighter conditions or temporary exit as two avenues.

sources.title: Schäuble insists that a 'temporary Grexit' is the best solution for Greece
Temporary Grexit had support in German govt. - Schaeuble

facts.claim: Coalition sources said the paper was drafted after discussions among Chancellor Merkel, Vice-Chancellor Gabriel and Schäuble, and that the preferred option was for Greece to reform and keep the euro.

sources.title: Schäuble insists that a 'temporary Grexit' is the best solution for Greece

facts.claim: On 14 July 2015 Schäuble said a temporary Grexit in the German offer had broad support, including within the federal government, and would have been a better solution for Greece.
facts.quote: many people, including in the federal government, were convinced the paper's approach would have been a much better solution for Greece

sources.title: Temporary Grexit had support in German govt. - Schaeuble

facts.claim: Accounts differ on whether Schäuble raised Grexit at the Eurogroup table; the five-year idea was discussed in the Brussels talks and widely rejected.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: 'proposed a temporary Grexit in 2015' is supported. 'Enforced austerity' is a characterisation; the specific conditionality figures on the page (22% minimum wage cut etc.) were not tested here.
